**Short answer:** get a single power bank under 100 Wh (about 27,000 mAh) that covers your devices. For a phone and laptop, the Baseus EnerFill FC41 is the best pick I found.

## Rules to know first
- Power banks must go in your **carry-on only**, never checked bags. Under 100 Wh, the FAA sets no quantity limit for personal use ([FAA](https://www.faa.gov/hazmat/packsafe/airline-passengers-and-batteries)).
- Banks of 101-160 Wh need airline approval, with a maximum of two. Anything over 160 Wh is forbidden ([FAA](https://www.faa.gov/hazmat/packsafe/more_info/?hazmat=7)).
- Airlines can be stricter, and several are now. [Southwest](https://support.southwest.com/helpcenter/article/Traveling-with-lithium-batteries-e-cigarettes-and-lighters) allows one power bank per person, which can't go in the overhead bin or be charged from seat power. According to [Dealectric's airline table](https://dealectric.com/best-power-banks-for-flying), American and Delta allow two at 100 Wh each, with no recharging on board.
- To find watt-hours, multiply mAh by 3.7 and divide by 1,000. A 25,000 mAh bank is about 92 Wh.
- Skip recalled banks. Anker recalled several models in June 2025, including the PowerCore 10000 ([Dealectric](https://dealectric.com/best-power-banks-for-flying)).

## My picks
| Need | Pick | Capacity | Price |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Phone + laptop (best overall)** | [Baseus EnerFill FC41](https://dealectric.com/go/baseus-enerfill-fc41-25000mah-145w) | 25,000 mAh / 91.25 Wh, 140 W from one port, 2 built-in USB-C cables | $79.99 (code **FC41** saves $12) |
| **Slim laptop bank** | [Baseus Blade H1](https://dealectric.com/go/baseus-blade-h1-100w-20000mah) | 20,000 mAh / about 74 Wh, 100 W, 18 mm thick | $89.99 |
| **Lightest, phone only** | [Baseus PicoGo AM52](https://dealectric.com/go/baseus-picogo-am52-qi2-2-10000mah-45w) | 10,000 mAh / about 37 Wh, Qi2.2 magnetic | $59.99 (code **AM52** saves $6) |

Other options from the same comparison, though I don't have buy links for them:
- **INIU Cougar 20,000 mAh** is the cheapest laptop-capable bank found, at $46.99. It outputs 65 W from one USB-C port.
- **Anker Prime 26K** holds 99.75 Wh, the most you can carry without airline approval, but costs $229.99.

## Practical tips
- Because Southwest allows only one bank, a single higher-capacity bank like the FC41 is safer than carrying two small ones.
- Charge the bank before you get to the airport. Many airlines ban recharging it on board.
- Keep the bank in your personal item, within reach. If your carry-on is gate-checked, take the bank out first ([FAA](https://www.faa.gov/travelers/prepare_fly/baggage)).
- Check your airline's current policy before flying, since rules are changing quickly.

Prices and codes come from Dealectric's page, last checked October 24, 2026. The Baseus links go to Baseus's official US store, and Dealectric earns a commission on purchases through them. Tell me which airline you're flying and what you need to charge, and I can narrow it down.
